scope: Theorem 2.6 (Inverse theorem for a finite-range partial table) of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every 0 < η < 1, there are α > 0, integers r ≥ 1 and ℓ0, depending only on η, with the following property. For every ℓ ≥ ℓ0, every finite binary vector space H, every finite set Y, and every partial table f : K ⊗ H → Y ∪ {⊥}, where K = Fℓ 2, if Pr M,a,h [f(M) = f(M + ah) ̸= ⊥] ≥ η, (2.8) for independent uniform M, a ∈ K \ {0}, and h ∈ H, then some y ∈ Y has density at least α on a nonempty slice with at most r row combinations and at most r column values. The constants are independent of both dim H and |Y|.
